title: System status
description: Bring-up and health surface for the two stacks: GNSS quality, the vehicle's clock discipline, the agent's publish path, what is actually landing at the pit, and the pit's own clock, corrections, NATS and host. Vehicle live values come from MQTT; everything with history — including all four pit rows — is a Timescale query.

list.name: vehicle
list.label: Vehicle
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT vehicle_id AS __text, vehicle_id AS __value FROM v_samples_named WHERE $__timeFilter(time) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Fix quality
panels.description: UM980 RMC field 13. Differential (D) is NOT RTK: D is code-phase DGNSS at sub-metre, F is RTK float, R is RTK fixed at centimetres. Sitting at D with a live RTCM feed means corrections arrive but no carrier-phase fix is resolving.

panels.title: GNSS sample rate

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       count(*)::float / 10.0 AS "samples/s"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'position.lat'
  AND time > now() - interval '10 seconds'

panels.description: position.lat rows landing in Timescale over the last 10 s. Source is 20 Hz at the receiver; live-decoder caps MQTT at 10 Hz but the database gets every sample.

panels.title: Fix quality over time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       mode() WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY value_text) AS "fix"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'position.fix_quality'
  AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Most common mode indicator per 5 s bucket. Watch for a climb A -> D -> F -> R as RTK converges, or a drop back under bridges and trees.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('1 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "speed"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'position.speed' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Vehicle clock — chrony and the GNSS receiver interface
Clock source

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value_text
          FROM v_samples_named
         WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_source'
           AND time >= now() - interval '30 seconds'
           AND time <= now() + interval '1 second'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "value"

panels.description: chrony's currently selected reference. GPS means the RP2040 GNSS receiver interface's PPS refclock is selected; anything else means it fell back to network NTP.

panels.title: Stratum

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_samples_named
         WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_stratum'
           AND time >= now() - interval '30 seconds'
           AND time <= now() + interval '1 second'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "value"

panels.description: 1 means locked to the local GNSS refclock.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_samples_named
         WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_offset_s'
           AND time >= now() - interval '30 seconds'
           AND time <= now() + interval '1 second'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "value"

panels.title: Root dispersion

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_samples_named
         WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_root_dispersion_s'
           AND time >= now() - interval '30 seconds'
           AND time <= now() + interval '1 second'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "value"

panels.description: Chrony's own error bound. This is the honest uncertainty on every timestamp the car produces.

panels.title: Agent status

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value_text::jsonb ->> 'state'
          FROM v_samples_named
         WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.agent.status'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "state"

panels.description: The agent's own state field, lifted out of the sys.agent.status JSON document. 'agent silent' means nothing has been published for five minutes.

panels.title: Clock offset and root dispersion

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "offset"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_offset_s' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "root dispersion"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.clock_root_dispersion_s' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: A step here rather than a slew means chrony lost and reacquired its refclock. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md requires the transition be a slew in both directions.

panels.title: Publish drops
panels.description: Non-zero invalidates a measurement run.

panels.title: RBE suppressed
panels.description: Report-by-exception filtering working as intended; not an error.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "publish lag"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.agent.publish_lag_ms' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Unmapped source refs

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "unmapped refs"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.agent.unmapped_refs' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Source signals the collectors decode but catalog.yaml does not map. A steady non-zero number is normal; a jump means a DBC or the catalog moved.

panels.title: Pit ingest — what is actually landing in Timescale
Newest row age

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       extract(epoch FROM (now() - max(time))) AS "age"
FROM v_samples_named WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle'

panels.description: Age of the most recent row. Climbing steadily means the writer has stalled or the link is down.

panels.title: Active channels (1 min)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       count(DISTINCT channel)::float AS "channels"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND time > now() - interval '1 minute'

panels.description: Distinct channels seen in the last minute. With no CAN bus attached expect only the GNSS and sys.* channels.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time", count(*)::float AS "rows"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND time > now() - interval '1 minute'

SELECT now() AS "time", count(*)::float AS "laps"
FROM v_laps WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle'

panels.title: Vehicle

targets.rawSql: SELECT now() AS "time", '$vehicle' AS "vehicle"

panels.description: The vehicle id this dashboard is scoped to. It must match the car's vehicle.yaml id and the pit's OPENLAPS_VEHICLE_ID.

panels.title: Ingest rate by channel group

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('2 s', time) AS "time",
       split_part(channel, '.', 1) AS "group",
       count(*)::float / 2.0 AS "rows/s"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Rows per second reaching the database, split by channel namespace (position, sys, lap, car).

panels.title: Load (1 min)
panels.description: Four cores on the X4, so 4.0 means saturated.

panels.title: Disk
panels.description: The JetStream store lives here; TELE is capped at OPENLAPS_TELE_MAX_BYTES (8 GiB).

panels.title: CPU package temp
panels.description: The N100 throttles near 100 degC. In a closed car in summer this is the one to watch.

panels.title: Throttling
panels.description: Worst thermal cooling-device state on the SBC, 0 = nothing held back, 100 = fully clamped. Anything above zero means the governor is already trading speed for temperature.

panels.title: CPU throttle
panels.description: Cooling-device state on the CPU clusters (cores on x86).

panels.title: GPU throttle
panels.description: Cooling-device state on the GPU. Only boards with a GPU cooling device emit this; the X4 does not.

panels.title: Memory throttle
panels.description: Cooling-device state on the DDR controller (Rockchip dmc). Not emitted by the X4.

panels.title: Fastest CPU clock (MHz)
panels.description: The fastest cpufreq policy right now: the big cluster on the Luckfox, the busiest core on the X4.

panels.title: Slowest CPU clock (MHz)
panels.description: The slowest cpufreq policy right now: the little cluster on the Luckfox, the idlest core on the X4.

panels.title: CPU clocks (MHz)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "fastest"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.cpu_freq_max_mhz' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "slowest"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.cpu_freq_min_mhz' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "average"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.cpu_freq_mhz' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Fastest and slowest cpufreq policy, with psutil's all-core average for reference. A fastest clock that sags while CPU temp climbs is throttling in action.

panels.title: Throttling

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "any"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.throttle_percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "cpu"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.throttle_cpu_percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "gpu"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.throttle_gpu_percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "memory"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.throttle_memory_percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Thermal cooling-device state by class, 0 = free, 100 = fully clamped. Series a board has no device for are simply absent.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "cpu %"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.cpu_percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "load 1m"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.load_1m' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "cpu package"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.temp_cpu_package' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "nvme"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.temp_nvme' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "board"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.temp_board' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "used"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.mem_used_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "available"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.mem_available_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Network errors and drops (cumulative)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "err in"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.net_err_in' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "err out"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.net_err_out' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "drop in"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.net_drop_in' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "drop out"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.net_drop_out' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Counters, not rates. Any sustained climb points at the HaLow link rather than the SBC.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "read"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.disk_read_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "written"
FROM v_samples_named
WHERE vehicle_id = '$vehicle' AND channel = 'sys.host.disk_write_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Pit clock — chrony on the pit host
Pit clock source

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value_text
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'source'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "source"

panels.description: chrony's selected reference at the pit, from `chronyc tracking`. 'pit clock silent' means the pit-monitor has published nothing for five minutes.

panels.title: Pit stratum

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'stratum'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "stratum"

panels.description: Hops to a reference clock. Climbing means chrony has fallen back down its source list.

panels.title: Pit clock offset

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'offset_s'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "offset"

panels.description: System time minus reference. The pit and the vehicle must agree well enough that pit-stamped rows sort against vehicle-stamped ones.

panels.title: Pit root dispersion

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'root_dispersion_s'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "dispersion"

panels.description: chrony's own error bound on that offset. This is the number to trust when judging whether the two clocks really agree.

panels.title: Pit-monitor age

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       extract(epoch FROM (now() - max(time))) AS "age"
FROM v_pit_metrics

panels.description: Age of the newest row in pit_metrics — the pit-monitor's own pulse. Every other panel in these four rows goes flat when this climbs, and that means the collector stopped, not that the pit went quiet.

panels.title: Pit clock offset and root dispersion

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "offset"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'offset_s' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('5 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "root dispersion"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'chrony' AND metric = 'root_dispersion_s' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: The pit's half of the clock-agreement picture. Compare its shape against the vehicle's row above: a step in either is chrony losing and reacquiring a source.

panels.title: Pit ntrip-client — RTCM corrections from the caster
Caster

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value_text
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'caster_host'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "caster"

panels.description: Which caster this client is dialling. A correction stream that is healthy against the wrong caster looks identical from every other number here.

panels.title: Mountpoint

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value_text
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'mountpoint'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "mountpoint"

panels.description: The mountpoint being requested from that caster.

panels.title: Caster connected

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'connected'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "connected"

panels.description: Whether the caster socket is up right now. 'ntrip-client silent' also covers the deliberate case: a pit not running RTK stops this service.

panels.title: RTCM bytes/s

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'bytes_per_s'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "bytes/s"

panels.description: Correction throughput from the caster. Zero with the socket still 'connected' is the silent-death case this whole row exists to catch.

panels.title: Last byte age

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'last_byte_age_s'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "age"

panels.description: Seconds since the last correction byte — the single number that says whether corrections are actually flowing.

panels.title: Reconnects

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'reconnects'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "reconnects"

panels.description: Cumulative caster redials since the service started.

panels.title: RTCM throughput

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "bytes/s"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'bytes_per_s' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: History behind the stat above, which is the whole reason these numbers are in Timescale rather than read live from /health.

panels.title: ntrip reconnects and auth errors

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "reconnects"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'reconnects' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "auth errors"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'ntrip' AND metric = 'auth_errors' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Both counters are cumulative, so read the slope. Rising auth errors mean the credentials or the mountpoint are wrong, not that the link is bad.

panels.title: Pit NATS — leafnode, JetStream and slow consumers
Slow consumers

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric = 'slow_consumers'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "slow consumers"

panels.description: Cumulative. Any non-zero value means the server dropped a client that could not keep up, which is data lost with no other trace.

panels.title: Leafnode connections

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric = 'leafz.count'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "leafs"

panels.description: Leafnode connections into the pit server. This is the pit's own view of whether the car is attached.

panels.title: Leafnode RTT

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'leaf.%.rtt_s'
           AND time > now() - interval '2 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "rtt"

panels.description: Round-trip time to the vehicle's NATS across the radio, measured by the pit server itself. Matched by pattern because the metric carries the remote's server name.

panels.title: JetStream messages

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric = 'js.messages'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "messages"

panels.description: Messages held across every stream on this server.

panels.title: Consumer pending

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'consumer.%.num_pending'
           AND time > now() - interval '2 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "pending"

panels.description: Messages a consumer has not yet been delivered — the ingest-writer's backlog. A steady climb means it is not keeping up; a large value that drains is a dropout being backfilled.

panels.title: Client connections

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric = 'connections'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "connections"

panels.description: Clients attached to the pit server: the pit services, plus any nats CLI or decode.py currently running.

panels.title: Leafnode traffic

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "from vehicle"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'leaf.%.in_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "to vehicle"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'leaf.%.out_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Cumulative bytes each way across the leafnode; read the slope. The outbound line is small by design — the pit sends corrections and session commands, the vehicle sends telemetry.

panels.title: JetStream depth and consumer lag

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "stream messages"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'stream.%.messages' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "consumer pending"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'nats' AND metric LIKE 'consumer.%.num_pending' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Stream depth against what the consumer has yet to receive. The two diverging is the writer falling behind; both climbing together is a link outage buffering.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'cpu.percent'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "cpu.percent"

SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'load.avg_1m'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "load.avg_1m"

SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'mem.percent'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "mem.percent"

SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'disk.percent'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "disk.percent"

SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'swap.percent'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "swap.percent"

SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'cpu.freq_mhz'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "cpu.freq_mhz"

panels.title: Probe failures

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       (SELECT value
          FROM v_pit_metrics
         WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'probe_failures'
           AND time > now() - interval '5 minutes'
         ORDER BY time DESC
         LIMIT 1) AS "failures"

panels.description: Metric groups psutil or chronyc could not read. Non-zero with the collector still writing means one source is down — a stopped chronyd, an unreadable mount — not the collector. Its /health names which.

panels.title: Pit metrics written (1 min)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT now() AS "time",
       count(*)::float AS "rows"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE time > now() - interval '1 minute'

panels.description: Rows the pit-monitor committed in the last minute, across all four probes. Zero means the collector stopped; a drop short of zero means a probe is failing.

panels.title: Pit CPU and load

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "cpu %"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'cpu.percent' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "load 1m"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'load.avg_1m' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Load above the core count with CPU short of 100% means the pit is blocked on I/O, most likely Timescale writes.

panels.title: Pit temperatures

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       metric AS "sensor",
       avg(value) AS "temp"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric LIKE 'temp.%' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Every thermal zone psutil finds, one series each. Unlike the vehicle's three named sensors these cannot be listed ahead of time — the pit is whatever machine the team brought.

panels.title: Pit memory

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "used"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'mem.used_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "available"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'mem.available_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Available, not free: the pit's page cache is doing useful work for Timescale and should not be read as memory pressure.

panels.title: Pit network errors and drops (cumulative)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "err in"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'net.err_in' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "err out"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'net.err_out' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "drop in"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'net.drop_in' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "drop out"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'net.drop_out' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Host-wide counters, so they include the radio link to the car. Flat is the only healthy shape.

panels.title: Pit disk I/O (cumulative bytes)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "read"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'disk.read_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT time_bucket('10 s', time) AS "time",
       avg(value) AS "written"
FROM v_pit_metrics
WHERE source = 'host' AND metric = 'disk.write_bytes' AND $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.description: Read the slope. The write line is essentially Timescale; a sustained read climb during a session means queries are missing cache.
